report:
Conclusion: the claim is best supported, not false. In the pivotal ZOE-70 randomized, placebo-controlled trial of adults ≥70, the adjuvanted recombinant zoster vaccine (HZ/su; Shingrix) significantly reduced herpes zoster and postherpetic neuralgia; the abstract states it “reduce[d] the risks” in this age group, with efficacy around 90% in pooled ≥70 analyses. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27626517/ and https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1603800

A later review of ZOE-50/ZOE-70 describes high efficacy and an acceptable serious-adverse-event profile, while noting injection-site/systemic reactogenicity. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7937016/

CDC recommends Shingrix/RZV to prevent shingles and complications in immunocompetent adults ≥50, which necessarily includes people ≥70. https://www.cdc.gov/shingles/hcp/vaccine-considerations/index.html

Caveats: protection is not 100%, two doses are needed, effectiveness can wane and may be lower in some immunocompromised groups, and short-lived fever, fatigue, myalgia, and injection-site pain are common. But the specific statement—that RZV reduces shingles in adults ≥70—is strongly evidence-based.
